budget.budgetBasis: maxima cover every probe being accepted; expectedWrites and expectedDeletes are the forecast under the expected outcome and bind nothing

recoveryWindow.authority: read-only unless the same run holds a conditional-creation proof and a matching version-bound ownership read
recoveryWindow.exitCondition: typed NOT_FOUND for every one of the 51 owned resources
recoveryWindow.onExhaustion: stop, leave the remaining resources recorded as unresolved, and escalate to the owner; never widen the scope or retry a Commit
recoveryWindow.trigger: any probe that reaches an observation failure, an uncertain Commit or an interrupted run

schedulingReservation.basis: shared_gate.create charges each slot requestSeconds plus intervalSeconds, refuses an interval below 0.25 and a wall above 1200, and refuses a recovery reservation below the recovery slots' cost.
schedulingReservation.enforcement: smallRequestSeconds is also the per-request timeout for a small read or delete, so a slot cannot outrun its own reservation; the boundary Commits keep the 60-second transport deadline.

cost.basis: Firestore Native published unit prices; a planning bound, not a billing record.
cost.networkNote: About 30 MiB is uploaded across the three Commits and under 1 MiB is returned. Ingress is not billed and the returned volume is negligible, so the network component of this campaign is zero to the published precision.

maximumUsage.basis: every probe accepted, which is the outcome the campaign exists to detect

note: The local shadow runs under these same bounds; production additionally requires the owner preconditions in fs-request-bytes-campaign.json. The maxima cover every probe being accepted; accounting is the forecast and binds nothing. budget.schedulingReservation closes the wall-clock arithmetic under shared_gate.create's formula.

transportDeadline.consequenceIfMissed: The receipt is incomplete, the Commit is uncertain, and the run holds no conditional-creation proof. The version-bound delete is then a zero-wire skip by design, so cleanup detects the residue as `cleanup-not-absent` but cannot remove it: up to 17 documents stay in the project pending manual owner action.
transportDeadline.covers: connection setup, TLS, the request upload, server processing and the bounded response read

derivation.marginNote: The published ceiling is that requirement with roughly a 2x margin.

transportDeadline.detection: Detected, never silent. The absence proofs are only recorded on a typed NOT_FOUND, so an unremovable residue fails the run rather than passing it.
enforcedBy: request_bytes_remote_transport.TIMEOUT, rejecting any larger timeout argument
request_bytes_https_worker, re-checking the same ceiling independently
transportDeadline.ownerAction: Run from a link that sustains the rate above. If a probe times out, the owner removes the residue under the recorded owned scope; the campaign never retries a Commit to compensate.
